River festival returns with a lantern parade after a year away

By Tomasz Okafor · 18 October 2026

The Linfield River Festival will return next month after a year away, with a lantern parade along both banks, boat races between the town's rowing clubs and a market on the old towpath, its organisers announced on Friday.

Last year's festival was called off when the river flooded the meadows where the stages usually stand. This year the main stage moves to the higher ground beside the cricket club, and the parade route has been shortened so that it stays on paths above the flood line.

More than six hundred lanterns are being made in workshops at the town's schools and community centres, many of them shaped like the fish, birds and boats that the river is known for. Anyone can join a workshop free of charge on the next three Saturdays.

The rowing races, which date back to 1902, will be held on the Sunday morning, and the organisers hope to add a race for children's crews if enough clubs take part. The towpath market will have stalls from local makers, bakers and growers.

Roads around the bridge will close from four in the afternoon on the evening of the parade, and extra buses will run from the station until midnight. The organisers ask people who live nearby to walk to the festival rather than drive.

The festival relies on volunteers to run it, and the committee is still looking for stewards for the parade and for people to help put up the stages. Volunteers get a festival T-shirt, a meal and the thanks of the whole town, its chair, Ruth Abernethy, said.
